content: In #31859, I introduced a definition of a point of a Grothendieck site and constructed the corresponding fiber functors on (pre)sheaves: the definition of a point was a nontrivial adaptation of SGA 4 IV 6.3 https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/be0a10d1f1d5c9434f47080fa0e2aa48b678ab3a/Mathlib/CategoryTheory/Sites/Point/Basic.lean#L62-L74. I have been developing this notion (and with Christian Merten, we constructed a conservative family of points for the étale site of a scheme #35136). In particular, I showed in #35572 that when the coefficient category is monoidal (and satisfy certains additional properties), fiber functors are monoidal, and in #35584, this allowed me to give a different proof of the properties that are required in order to show that a category of sheaves is monoidal: it suffices that the site has enough points.

I have extended this to (pre)sheaves of modules. In the draft PR #35773, I give a different approach to the module structure on stalks, by providing a slightly different construction of a colimit of modules over a filtered inductive system of rings, and in the case of commutative rings, I show that this colimit defines a monoidal functor. In particular, the fiber functor on presheaves of modules given by a point of the site is a monoidal functor, and in a similar fashion as I obtained that categories of sheaves with values in a monoidal category tend to be monoidal, I have shown that if the site has enough points, then the category of sheaves of modules over a commutative sheaf of rings is monoidal.

In particular, if X is a scheme, the category of OX\mathcal O_XOX​-Modules is monoidal https://github.com/joelriou/mathlib4/blob/presheaf-of-modules-point/Mathlib/AlgebraicGeometry/Modules/Monoidal.lean
With some additional efforts, it should be possible to verify that the full subcategory of quasi-coherent sheaves is also monoidal.
